newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: PM PAYS TRIBUTE TO DENG XIAOPING
Prime Minister John Howard says it will be interesting to watch any re-alignment of power influences in China following the death of that country's paramount leader, Deng Xiaoping.
Mr Howard paid tribute to the 93-year-old man who was responsible for modernising China's economy.
Speaking on Sydney Radio 2-G-B Mr Howard says despite not having held any formal position for some time, Deng remained influential until his death...and his legacy will live on.
He says he doesn't expect great change to relations between China and the rest of the world in the wake of Deng's death.
EXTRADITION RULING WELCOMED BY GOVERNMENT
The Federal Government has welcomed the ruling by a South African magistrate that the legal requirements for the extradition of alleged paedophile Philip Bell, have been met.

The Attorney-General, Daryl Williams, says he understands the matter is now expected to go before South African authorities, who have responsibility for determining whether Mr Bell should be surrendered to Australia.
Mr Williams says under South African law Mr Bell has 15 days in which to lodge an appeal against the magistrate's ruling.
AIRLINE GROUNDING A "POLITICAL WHIM" OF CASA: DIRECTOR
The Civil Aviation Safety Authority has been accused of acting on a political whim after grounding a North Queensland airline yesterday.
Director of the Wingz North airline, Gary Maile, claims the Authority is under pressure because of its current row with the Federal Government over the effectiveness of the Authority's board.
The Authority claims it has identified serious safety deficiencies in the airline's operations.
But Mr Maile's denied the claims saying the faults picked up were superficial, involving trivial administrative details or minor equipment checks which would not have jeopardised passenger safety.
BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF JUDICIARY NEEDED: WILLIAMS
Federal Attorney General Daryl Williams says a better understanding of the judiciary in the community would change the position of some in the current debate over the role of the High Court.
Mr Williams says the debate highlights the need for civics, and government in general, to be taught in schools.
He says the judiciary is one of the least well understood parts of society.
The Attorney General says the debate is not unique to Australia with similiar questioning of the judiciary's role going on in England and the United States.
STRIKE THREATS DISMISSED BY REITH
Threats of a national strike from the ACTU have been described as old fashioned rhetoric by the Federal Industrial Relations Minister.
The ACTU says that if the Government's May Budget increased the age workers could claim their superannuation from 55 years to 60, it would call the strike.
Peter Reith told ABC Radio that such a change was the 1992 policy position of the ALP, and didn't attract the same threats at the time.
He says any changes to superannuation will be decided on their merit, not under vague threats of industrial action.
QLD PREMIER WANTS PROCLAMATIONS ON HINCHINBROOK LIFTED
Queensland Premier Rob Borbidge says it's unacceptable that resort developer Keith Williams keeps having to face legal challenges over his Port Hinchinbrook resort development in North Queensland.
Mr Borbidge says the Federal Environment Minister should act responsibly and lift World Heritage-based proclamations relating to the development.
He says they make it extremely difficult for the project to proceed, and provide a mechanism for the validity of the project and its approvals to be questioned.
The Premier says the proclamations were put in place by Labor in 1994, and were politically motivated.
But, Hinchinbrook campaign co-ordinator, David Haigh, says the proclamations are vital because without them a total devastation would have occured.
KENNETT HAS CONFIDENCE IN POLICE MINISTER
Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett says police minister Bill McGrath, was "being honest", when he expressed great reservations about gays in the force.
Mr Kennett says he has full confidence in Mr McGrath, and wasn't angered or embarrassed by his comments on the ABC's 7-30 Report.
He says Mr McGrath has a right to express his opinion, and has dismissed calls for the minister's resignation as "ridiculous".
NEW LEADER IN SYDNEY GOLF CHALLENGE
Chris Gray is the new leader in the first round of the Canon Challenge at Sydney's Terrey Hills course.
Gray is three under par after eight holes, a shot clear of seven players on two under.
The chasing pack comprises Tsuyoshi Yomeyama, Peter Senior, Mike Harwood, Scott Laycock, Lindsay Stephen, Martin Ayres and Tony Carolan.
